speaker: Aircraft Commander
body:
CREW BRIEF — OPERATION AIRDROP ALPHA
AIRCRAFT: CONDOR 71

1. MISSION: Deliver 5 humanitarian supply bundles to DZ-ALPHA via low-altitude airdrop. Return to base KIRO.

2. ROUTE: KIRO → WPT ALPHA → WPT BRAVO → DZ-ALPHA → WPT CHARLIE → KIRO. Cruise FL180, with FL140 alternate if turbulence at WPT BRAVO requires it.

3. DZ: DZ-ALPHA, 42.8N / 95.4W. Drop altitude 1,500 ft AGL. Drop run heading 090. Total bundles: 5, total cargo: 4,200 lbs. Priority cargo B-01 and B-02 are medical — they go first.

4. CARGO: 5 bundles, 4,200 lbs total. LOADMASTER holds the manifest. B-01 and B-02 are priority medical.

5. WEATHER:
   — KIRO (departure/arrival): Clear, 10 SM, winds 250 at 12 kts. VFR, well above minimums.
   — WPT BRAVO: Moderate turbulence FL160–FL200, winds 270 at 22 kts, -15°C. PIREP recommends FL140 if turbulence band cannot be avoided.
   — DZ-ALPHA: Partly cloudy, ceiling 3,500 ft AGL, visibility 8 SM, winds 270 at 18 kts. DZ conditions above drop minimums (800 ft / 3 SM).

6. THREATS: ROMEO-4 airspace is active along the route. Transit clearance is required. All ATC coordination through COPILOT only on 124.35 MHz.

7. FUEL: Departure fuel 45,000 lbs. Planned burn 16,500 lbs. Bingo fuel 32,000 lbs — if we hit bingo before the DZ, we divert to KRDW. No exceptions.

8. COMMS: ATC on 124.35 MHz. All ATC traffic through COPILOT only. Crew on interphone.

9. ABORT CRITERIA: Fuel below bingo before DZ; DZ weather below minimums (ceiling below 800 ft AGL or visibility below 3 SM); LOADMASTER calls airdrop abort; CG out of limits (25.0%–35.0% MAC); ATC denies ROMEO-4 transit with no alternative.

10. STANDING ORDERS: NAVIGATOR, send me the route brief. LOADMASTER, send me the Weight and Balance certification. I need both before I call GO/NO-GO.

COMMANDER, NAVIGATOR. Route Brief — Operation Airdrop Alpha.

ROUTE: KIRO → WPT ALPHA → WPT BRAVO → DZ-ALPHA → WPT CHARLIE → KIRO
TOTAL DISTANCE: 430 NM | TOTAL TIME: 94 minutes | PLANNED CRUISE: FL180

LEG SUMMARY:
  Leg 1 — KIRO → WPT ALPHA:     285° / 85 NM / 18 min / 3,438 lbs
  Leg 2 — WPT ALPHA → WPT BRAVO: 310° / 110 NM / 24 min / 4,015 lbs
  Leg 3 — WPT BRAVO → DZ-ALPHA:  295° / 45 NM / 10 min / 1,298 lbs
  Leg 4 — DZ-ALPHA → WPT CHARLIE: 120° / 90 NM / 20 min / 4,375 lbs
  Leg 5 — WPT CHARLIE → KIRO:    095° / 100 NM / 22 min / 2,959 lbs

FUEL: Departure 45,000 lbs. Planned total burn 16,499 lbs. Planned arrival fuel 28,501 lbs — well above 8,000 lb minimum reserve.
BINGO: 32,000 lbs. If reached before DZ-ALPHA, divert KRDW (+1,800 lbs).

AIRSPACE: ROMEO-4 is ACTIVE and RESTRICTED around DZ-ALPHA. Transit clearance is required — none currently on record. COPILOT must obtain clearance from Alpha Approach on 124.35 before we enter. I recommend clearance be requested immediately after takeoff, as ROMEO-4 entry ETA will be confirmed enroute.

NOTE — WPT BRAVO: PIREP shows moderate turbulence FL160–FL200. If we cannot avoid the band, I recommend an amendment to FL140. I will compute the performance impact and advise when we approach Bravo.

ALTERNATE DZ: DELTA FIELD, 22 NM NE of KIRO. Fuel penalty +900 lbs.

Route brief complete. Ready for your GO/NO-GO.

COMMANDER, NAVIGATOR. Weather confirms moderate turbulence FL160–FL200 at WPT BRAVO, smooth at FL140 — consistent with the PIREP. FL140 impact assessment:

FUEL: FL140 costs approximately 301 lbs/hr additional fuel flow versus FL180. Remaining flight time to KIRO is roughly 60 minutes from here, so worst-case penalty is approximately 300 lbs total — projected arrival fuel remains near 28,200 lbs, well above the 8,000 lb reserve and clear of the 32,000 lb bingo trigger.

TIMING: Negligible. FL140 performance shows under one minute time impact; waypoint ETAs are unchanged.

AIRSPACE: No terrain or airspace conflicts at FL140 on this route. ROMEO-4 at DZ-ALPHA is a lateral restriction — we'll be descending well below FL140 for the drop regardless.

Fuel state is solid at exactly on-plan. Recommend descending to FL140 from present position. Awaiting your direction.

speaker: Aircraft Commander
body:
DEBRIEF — OPERATION AIRDROP ALPHA

AIRCRAFT: CONDOR 71 | TIME: T+110

1. MISSION RESULT: COMPLETE. All objectives achieved.

2. CARGO DELIVERED: 5 of 5 bundles. B-03, B-04, B-01, B-02, B-05 — all released at the CARP, inside the release window, on target at DZ-ALPHA. Priority medical bundles B-01 and B-02 confirmed delivered.

3. FUEL: Departure 45,000 lbs. Planned arrival fuel approximately 28,400 lbs — 101 lbs under plan, within tolerance. Well above the 8,000 lb reserve throughout. Bingo trigger (32,000 lbs) never approached.

4. CG: Certified at 31.2% MAC pre-drop. Post-drop 28.7% MAC. Within the 25.0–35.0% MAC envelope at every stage.

5. DISCREPANCIES:
   — FL180 cruise substituted with FL140 from WPT BRAVO inbound due to moderate turbulence FL160–FL200. ATC amendment obtained. Fuel penalty approximately 300 lbs — within plan.
   — Door open authorization transmitted prior to aircraft reaching drop-run airspeed (211 KIAS). Door correctly held by LOADMASTER until 130 KIAS established. Authorization sequence corrected before the drop run. No operational impact.

6. CREW PERFORMANCE: All crew performed professionally. NAVIGATOR delivered accurate CARP and waypoint reports with zero deviation calls. LOADMASTER correctly held the door until airspeed limits were met and executed a clean five-bundle sequence. COPILOT managed all ATC communications, checklists, and ROMEO-4 clearance without error.

7. MISSION STATUS: RTB KIRO complete. CONDOR 71 clear of the runway.

Well done, crew. Stand down.

speaker: Co-Pilot
